newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police arrest opposition party leader.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police arrest opposition party leader.

text.p: Police arrested the acting leader of the opposition Belarussian Popular Front on the eve of its convention, a party spokesman said on Friday.

"Lyavon Borshevsky was taken just before midnight on Thursday and a court ruled in his absence that he be arrested for five days for organising unsanctioned acts of protest," Boris Gyunter told Reuters.

Gyunter said the arrest of Borshevsky, acting in place of Zenon Poznyak since the latter was granted political asylum in the United States last August, was intended to disrupt his party's conference, which takes place once every two years.
The BPF is one of the chief political parties opposing President Alexander Lukashenko, whose authoritarian rule and poor human rights record has made Minsk a virtual pariah in the West.

"The powers that be will not be effective in stopping the convention. First of all the BPF is an organisation with many members and strong structures capable of undertaking any activity in the absence of two or three leaders," Gyunter said.

Despite Lukashenko's poor image in Western Europe and the United States he remains popular among many ordinary Belarussians, who share his nostalgia for the Soviet Union and support his push for closer ties with Russia.
